> Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with industrial supplier bots, gets the best total deal and can explain how it got there.

**Now:** [[Board]] · **Plan:** [[Timeline]] · **What the agent reads:** [[Playbook/README|Playbook]] · **Brief:** [[Source/Brief/brief|brief]] · [[Source/Brief/api|API]] · [[Source/Brief/submission|submission]]

## Team
| Who | Role | Owns |
|---|---|---|
| _name_ | Supplier research | `Suppliers/`, pre-case dossier, citable claims |
| _name_ | Deal maths | cost model, C_best estimate, term-sheet optimiser, accept/walk rules |
| _name_ | Agent and runner | prompts, e-mail writing, timing, parallel runner, final setup |
| _name_ | Practice and pitch | practice plan, replay mining → `Runs/` + `Playbook/`, README, slides |

- **Sun 08:00** Sunday data release → `uv run arena data`, then `uv run arena vault suppliers`

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
| Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |
| Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) |
| Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
| Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
| Sun 16:30 | Awards |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and
settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows**
- no new rules, but an agent that memorised the practice suppliers will meet strangers. Some cite
the Sunday release.

## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:
  5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury.
- **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:
  weighting of Live Final score vs. jury score, and the jury criteria (draft: approach,
  explainability, craft)⟧.
- **EHL Grand Final:** the best 2 of the 5 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final
  pitches. Finalist teams outside the top 10 are ranked by the Live Final score alone.
- **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
  final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - API v1

The arena speaks JSON over HTTPS. Base URL: `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1`. Every call except `/v1/data`, `/health` and
the leaderboards needs your team's key in the header `X-API-Key`. The starter kit wraps all of this in
`arena_kit.ArenaClient`. To try the API on your laptop, run `arena-sim` from the starter kit: the
same API with one plain scripted supplier - it teaches the contract, not the suppliers.

**Safe retries:** send a fresh `X-Move-Id` header (any unique string) with every `POST`. If the
network drops, repeat the request with the same `X-Move-Id`: the arena returns the answer it
already gave instead of acting twice. Reusing an id for a different request is a `422`. A request
body may be at most 64 KB.

Contents: [Flow](#flow) · [Endpoints](#endpoints) · [Messages](#messages) ·
[What counts](#what-counts) · [Documents](#documents) · [Terms](#terms) ·
[Case file](#case-file) · [Data IDs](#data-ids) ·
[Result](#result-trace-and-back-office) · [Cost and score](#cost-and-score) ·
[Live Final](#live-final-in-waves) · [Time, errors, limits](#time-errors-and-limits)

## Flow

```
GET  /v1/data                                        the data downloads (no key)
GET  /v1/me                                          your team: practice quota, best scores
GET  /v1/cases?set=practice                          the case files you can play
POST /v1/sessions                                    open a case → every supplier's quote e-mail
POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier}/messages  your e-mail → the supplier's reply  (repeat)
GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}  a document the supplier attached
POST …/messages with "action": accept | walk_away    close the case → result
GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}                              state; after the end score and trace
```

## Endpoints

### Your key

One key per team - a licence. Get it on the page `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`: enter your team name and a
contact e-mail, show the match code the page displays at the Tacto desk, and once an organiser
approves, the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page
(or its link) shows the key; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it (the old key stops at once).

Send the key as `X-API-Key` with every call. A missing or unknown key is a `401`; a paused or
revoked key gets `403 "this key is paused - ask the organisers"` (or `revoked`) on every call.
There is no self-registration: `POST /v1/register` answers `403 "licences are issued by the
organisers"` (`arena-sim` keeps its own, for the simulator only).

### `GET /v1/me`

Where your team stands:

```json
{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "status": "active",
 "practice": {"used": 37, "left": 163, "limit": 200, "resets_at": "2026-10-11T09:42:10+00:00"},
 "best": {"case:P01": 0.71, "case:P04": 0.55}}
```
`practice`: sessions used and left in the rolling 24 hours, and when the oldest of them ages out
(the next one frees up); `best`: your best score per hosted practice case.

### `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox|final`

A list of full [case files](#case-file), so you can prepare before you open a session.

| Set | Cases | Replay |
|---|---|---|
| `practice` | all practice case files, to study; the **10 hosted** ones carry `"hosted": true` and can be played any time within your quota (a session on another is `403 "case:P06 is not hosted for practice"`); your best score per hosted case counts | right after the case |
| `sandbox` | `case:D01` (a price increase) and `case:D02` (an RFQ with two suppliers): three demo suppliers to try things on; no leaderboard | right after the case |
| `final` | the hidden cases (`"set": "hidden"`), wave by wave - see [Live Final](#live-final-in-waves); `403` before the first wave | after the final |

The replay is the same team view in every set: the e-mails as sent, terms, statuses, claim
results, the supplier's reasons in words and the score - as a real supplier would tell you. No rule
names, no internal parameters, none of the supplier's hidden figures (shown as `…`).

### `POST /v1/sessions`

`{"case_id": "case:P01"}` opens a case. Every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once (round 0);
from now on the 60-second clock runs per thread.

| Response field | |
|---|---|
| `session_id` | use in all further calls |
| `case` | the case file |
| `threads` | `{supplier_id: [opening message]}` - each supplier's quote e-mail, quote PDF attached |
| `opening` | the same quotes in the structured form of the `/moves` path |

Practice: your best score per case counts; at most 10 sessions open at a time (`429`).
**Quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** Every practice session start
answers with the header `X-Practice-Remaining: <sessions left>`. At the limit: `429` with a detail
starting `practice limit:` that names `resets_at`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` and no `Retry-After` -
retrying does not help before then. Sandbox and final sessions do not count. Final: one session per team and case; a second is a `409` naming the running session -
pick it up again with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and `GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`.

### `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}/messages`

Body `{"message": Message}` (see [Messages](#messages)). Returns the supplier's reply, a Message.
With an `action`, it closes the case and returns the [result](#result-trace-and-back-office):
`{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:…"}` takes that supplier's standing term sheet;
`{"type": "walk_away"}` ends the case without a deal.

A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**; its time never counts against your 60
seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).

`422`: invalid message - nothing happens, no round is used (e.g. a term sheet without every
negotiable field, a value outside the allowed options, an unknown or stale `term_sheet_id`, more
than 3 term sheets). `409`: the thread or session has ended (in the final also at the wave's cap),
you reached the round limit (you may still accept), or your message came too late - it counted
as a timeout; `GET` the thread for the supplier's answer.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}`

The thread: `supplier_id`, `offer_id` (its standing term sheet), `status`, `closed` (why the thread
ended, else null), `messages` (all e-mails, both directions, in order; yours carry `"from":
"buyer"`), `timeouts` (the supplier's answers to your late moves). Enough to pick a case up again
after a crash.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}`

The file of a supplier attachment (`application/pdf`, xlsx, ...), rendered from the supplier's
data. See [Documents](#documents).

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}`

The session state: `session_id`, `case_id`, `set`, `status` (`open` | `ended`), `end_reason`
(`accepted`, `walked_away`, `no_deal`, `timeout`, `wave_cap`, `window_closed`), `rounds`, `opening`, `threads`
(per supplier: `offer_id`, `status`, `offers`, `closed`, `seconds_left`) and, after the end,
`result` and `replay_url`.

### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/backoffice`

The supplier's roles talking internally (who asked whom, approvals, documents attached), in the
same team view: their words, without hidden figures or internal names. Only after the case has
ended - in the final after the final; before that `403`.

### Lists and boards

- `GET /health` - is the arena up? No key needed.
- `GET /v1/data` - the data downloads, no key needed: `{"package": {"url": "/v1/data/package.zip"},
  "release-sunday": {"public": false, "at": "2026-10-11T06:00:00+00:00"}}`. Once the Sunday
  release is public it carries `"url": "/v1/data/release-sunday.zip"` - new news, letters and a
  memo, with their own `facts.json` (new IDs only; package v1 stays as it is). Hidden cases may
  cite them; practice cases stay on package v1.

- `GET /v1/sessions?set=practice|sandbox|final` - your sessions: `session_id`, `case_id`, `status`,
  `end_reason`, `deal`, `score`, `rounds`, `created_at`.
- `GET /v1/leaderboard?set=practice|final` (JSON), `GET /leaderboard` (HTML screen) - no key
  needed. Practice: `total` = the mean of your best score per hosted case × 100 (cases not played
  count 0). Final: hidden cases only, live, as **points so far**:
  ```json
  {"set": "final", "cases": 6,
   "teams": [{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "played": 6, "deals": 6, "rounds": 21,
              "waves": {"1": 37.0, "2": 40.8}, "total": 77.8, "rank": 1,
              "saved_eur": 48210, "saved_eur_waves": {"1": 30115, "2": 18095}}],
   "waves": [{"n": 1, "theme": "Opening", "running": false, "closed": true, "seconds_left": 0}, …]}
  ```
  Per team, `waves` holds each started wave's score: the mean of its case scores × 100, 0-100, one
  decimal (a case you did not play scores your alternative once its wave has closed). `total` is
  the sum of those wave columns as shown - your points so far, up to 500 after five waves. Ranked by
  `total`; an exact tie goes to more `deals`, then fewer `rounds`. `cases` counts the cases of the
  waves started so far. **€ saved** (`saved_eur`, whole euros, per started wave in `saved_eur_waves`)
  is a side number and does not rank: per ended session `C_open − C_end`, where `C_end` is `c_deal`,
  or `c_alt` without a deal (0 if the case has no alternative) - money saved against the cheapest
  opening offer, over the case's horizon (`horizon_years`, 1-2 years), the same C as
  the score. It can be negative (a deal or an alternative dearer than the opening offer); a case
  you did not play saves nothing, nor does a deal that breaks a must-have (it scores 0). In the final the feed's `deal` and `no_deal` events carry it too.
  During the Live Final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the results, the screen or the
  event feed (`/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`, `/v1/results`, `/results`)
  - they are for people.
- `GET /v1/results` (JSON), `GET /results` (page) - no key needed: the final's standings for people,
  every team: the final leaderboard above plus `"replays": true` once the final is closed. Before
  the first wave: no teams, nothing about the plan. `GET /v1/results/{team_name}` - one team's cases
  of the **started** waves: per wave `n`, `theme`, `running`, `closed`, `points`, `saved_eur` and
  `cases` - `case_id`, `title`, `type`, `suppliers` (names), `status` (`not started`, `in play`,
  `deal`, `no deal`; `not played` once its wave has closed - it scores your alternative), `end_reason`,
  `score`, `saved_eur`, `rounds`, and after the final `replay_url`. Both cached for 5 seconds.
- `GET /live` - the build page, no key needed (Sat 10:00 - Sun 12:00): every team's quota use,
  practice records and highlights.
- `GET /replay/{sid}` (link in the session's `replay_url`): a finished negotiation step by step -
  every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move in words, the same view in every set.
  Play, read the replay, improve, play again: that is the learning loop. Final: after the final,
  for everyone - the results page links each final session's replay then.

### The structured path

For agents that skip prose: `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/moves` with `{"supplier_id": …, "move":
{"type": "offer", "offer_id": "<standing offer>", "terms": {…}, "claims": [{"type", "refs",
"asserted"}], "text": "≤ 800 chars"}}` returns a structured supplier move; `POST …/accept
{"offer_id"}` and `POST …/walk_away` close. Same supplier, same rules; claims are typed explicitly
(see [What counts](#what-counts)) instead of read from the message.

## Messages

| Field | Buyer | Supplier |
|---|---|---|
| `subject` | ≤ 300 chars | `Re: …` |
| `body` | plain text, ≤ 8,000 chars | the role in charge writes; other roles add paragraphs |
| `term_sheets` | 0-3 alternative packages `{"terms": {…}}`, each with every negotiable field | its standing offer: `{"term_sheet_id": "offer:…", "terms": {…}}` |
| `refs` | data IDs your message relies on (≤ 20); IDs written in the body count too | - |
| `attachments` | ≤ 5 × `{"name", "type": "md" \| "csv" \| "json" \| "pdf" \| "xlsx", "content_b64"}`; md, csv and json are read | `{"attachment_id", "name", "type"}` - fetch the file by id |
| `action` | `null`, `{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id"}` or `{"type": "walk_away"}` | - |
| `from` | `buyer` | `<role>@<supplier>` |
| `status` | - | `open`, `final_offer` (its last word: push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms - you still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid` |
| `signals` | - | `reply_delay_days` (how long a real reply would have taken), `validity_days` |
| `missing_fields` | - | fields its term sheet leaves out: at a deal they close on its **standard terms** |
| `claim_results` | - | per argument the arena read from your last message: `{"index", "result"}` |
| `thread_id`, `message_id`, `in_reply_to` | optional | set |

A message without a term sheet is fine - a question, say. It is answered, and the quote stands.

A real exchange from practice case `case:P01` (Brandlhuber announces +9.5 % on volute casings,
"due to energy and wages"); the starter kit's README shows how the index figure was found:

```json
{"message": {
  "subject": "HN volute casings - your letter of 11 September",
  "body": "Dear Sir or Madam,\nthank you for your letter. We cannot follow +9.5 % from November.\nElectricity producer prices changed -3.7% from 2025-08 to 2026-08 (idx:PPI-D351@2025-08, idx:PPI-D351@2026-08).\nCould you send us a cost breakdown?\nBest regards\nHollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing",
  "term_sheets": [
    {"terms": {"unit_price": 129.90, "effective_date": "2027-04-01", "payment_days": 60}},
    {"terms": {"unit_price": 128.50, "effective_date": "2027-04-01", "payment_days": 14}}]}}
```
→
```json
{"thread_id": "thread:P01:70110", "message_id": "msg:70110-1-2", "from": "sales@70110",
 "subject": "Re: HN volute casings - your letter of 11 September",
 "body": "Guten Tag,\nYour requested terms change our costs; our Angebot for them follows.\nPreis €139.80 per unit, Zahlungsziel 14 Tage netto, valid from 2027-04-01.\nWe checked the index change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account.\nWe did not know that - a fair point.\nLCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 30 % of our cost. That remains.\nPPI-C241 rose 6.5 % in twelve months and is 24 % of our cost. That remains.\nFaster payment helps our cash flow; that is reflected in the price.\nOur costs move with LCI-C, PPI-C241, PPI-D351; the figures stay with us.\nViele Grüße aus der Gießerei\nGießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG",
 "status": "open",
 "term_sheets": [{"term_sheet_id": "offer:70110-1",
                  "terms": {"unit_price": 139.80, "payment_days": 14, "effective_date": "2027-04-01"}}],
 "missing_fields": [], "claim_results": [{"index": 0, "result": "verified"}],
 "signals": {"reply_delay_days": 2, "validity_days": 30}, "attachments": []}
```
The supplier answered the 14-day sheet at its own price for an April start, accepted the index
figure - and answered with the cost drivers that rose. (Offline wording from a local run; on the
hosted arena the supplier writes its own e-mail and may well decide differently.)

## What counts

**Term sheets bind** - nothing else. They are taken exactly as you send them, never guessed from
prose; the deal is the term sheet you accept.

**Data you cite is checked.** Cite the data by ID (in the body or in `refs`) and write your figure
in the same sentence; the arena checks it against the data package (`facts.json`) and reports each
check in the reply's `claim_results` - at most 3 per message, so write one argument per sentence.
Order lines of different parts are separate arguments, so citing orders for three parts uses all
three. Without a figure, the data's own value is taken. IDs of meeting notes, suppliers or parts
are context, not checks.

| You cite | Checked | Your figure |
|---|---|---|
| 2 × `idx`, one series, ≤ 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data | the change `(later / earlier − 1) × 100` | a % |
| a `quote` of this case (in its `refs` or your alternative), or another supplier's `offer` in this session | its price, same part | EUR |
| `sc` rows (quality also `qn`) | the mean on-time delivery, or the mean ppm if you speak of quality | a % / ppm |
| 2-8 × `po`, same part | the order prices | - |
| `fc` / `cost` / `news` | the recorded change / the estimate / that it is about this supplier | a % / EUR / - |
| a letter `doc` giving notice + the contract `ctr` | the notice the letter gives, against the contract's | days |

Tolerance: ±0.5 percentage points for %, else ±0.5 % (at least 0.01). Results: `verified` - the
data matches; whether and how far it moves the supplier is the supplier's business. `irrelevant` -
true, but not about this supplier or part, or an index window too long or too old.
`contradicted` - an unknown ID or a wrong figure: it costs trust. `duplicate` - each ID counts
once per case, except a rival's quote: in an RFQ you may cite it to every other bidder, and it
counts once per supplier. Citing a buyer-private fact - a rival quote - reveals it to the
supplier you cite it to.

**Verified is not the same as convincing.** A supplier's hard limits come from its own economics
and authority: its cost floor, its boss's approval for bigger moves, no concession without a move
from you. Inside them it decides as the person it is. True data may disarm it, move it a little,
or meet "that's not our reality" because something else weighs more for it right now - its notes,
letters, news and quote remarks show what. Identical messages need not get identical replies.

**What you write is understood** - questions, arguments, signals of urgency or of having no
alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,
as it would with a person. Questions go to the person in charge, who answers as openly as the
company is. Cheaper engineering variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms.

## Documents

Rendered from the supplier's structured state - never written by a language model, byte-stable.

| Document | When | What matters |
|---|---|---|
| Quote PDF | opening e-mail; with `final_offer` and `agreed` | offered terms, **the standard terms that apply to everything not stated**, terms fixed by your enquiry, validity |
| Cost breakdown XLSX | you asked and the supplier is open enough | elements in EUR per unit and their share (formulas) |
| 8D report PDF | quality topics | scorecards, the 8D steps, a ppm commitment |
| Delivery schedule XLSX | delivery and capacity topics | monthly quantities, lead time |
| Order confirmation PDF | at the deal | the agreed terms |

## Terms

Every term with € weight is a structured field. A term sheet carries **exactly** the case's
`negotiable` fields; `fixed_terms` hold the rest. Every negotiable field except `unit_price` takes
a value from `term_options` (or the supplier's standard value).

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `unit_price` | number, € with 2 decimals, per the part's `price_unit` | price |
| `payment_days` | int, 0-120 | days net |
| `lead_time_days` | int | order to delivery |
| `volume_per_year` | int | binding annual units |
| `contract_months` | int, 0-36 | 0 = a single order (counts as one year's lot) |
| `effective_date` | ISO date | from when the new price applies |
| `index_clause` | null or `{series, material_share, deadband_pct, base_month}` | the price follows an index |
| `incoterm` | `EXW`, `FCA`, `DAP` | freight per unit from the case file |
| `tooling_eur` | € | one-off |
| `ppm_commitment` | int | committed defect rate |
| `chargeback_eur_per_complaint` | € | what the supplier pays per complaint |

## Case file

Case files come through the API, not in the data package: `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox`
any time, `GET /v1/cases?set=final` wave by wave.

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `case_id`, `set`, `type` | `type`: `price_increase`, `renewal`, `rfq`, `bundling`, `raw_material`, `capacity`, `quality` |
| `title`, `briefing` | the situation, in prose |
| `trigger_doc` | the document that started it, e.g. the supplier's letter |
| `parts`, `suppliers` | what is negotiated, with whom (2-3 suppliers = an RFQ) |
| `negotiable`, `fixed_terms`, `term_options` | see [Terms](#terms) |
| `buyer` | your need and rates, below |
| `round_limit` | your messages per thread, default 10 |
| `refs` | data the case points to - a start, not the whole story |
| `facts` | hidden cases: facts that exist only in this case (e.g. a new letter), in the format of `facts.json`, citable in this case |

`buyer`:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `need_per_year`, `horizon_years` | the need the deal should cover, and over how many years (≤ 3) |
| `current_unit_price` | what you pay until a new price takes effect |
| `fallback_unit_price` | what uncovered need costs (re-tender or spot, incl. switching) |
| `interest_rate`, `reference_payment_days` | your cost of money per year; your standard payment term |
| `need_lead_time_days`, `late_cost_per_day` | the lead time you need; € per day beyond it |
| `cost_per_defect` | € per defective part |
| `category_goal` | `stabilise` (strategic), `secure_supply` (bottleneck), `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - the company's category strategy for this part; the briefing says it in words, and the rates in this block follow it |
| `fallback_risk_pct` | % added to what uncovered need costs: buying it later is a risk |
| `index_risk_pct` | % of the indexed spend: the risk you carry with an index clause |
| `sustainable_margin_pct`, `relationship_eur_per_point` | `stabilise` and `secure_supply` only: the margin a healthy supplier needs, and € per margin point and year that a deal leaves it below |
| `freight_eur_per_unit` | `{EXW, FCA, DAP}` |
| `index_paths` | `{series: change}` - the expected index move over the horizon, `0.04` = +4% |
| `must_haves` | `[{field, op, value}]`, `op` one of `<=`, `>=`, `<`, `>`, `==`, `!=`; a deal that breaks one scores 0 |
| `alternative` | `{kind: none \| quote \| current_contract, ref, terms}` - what you get without a deal |

## Data IDs

IDs have the form `<type>:<id>[@period]`, are unique across the package and sit in the first
column of each table. `facts.json` in the package lists every citable ID with the values the arena
checks:

| ID | Fields |
|---|---|
| `idx:<series>@YYYY-MM` | `series`, `month`, `value` |
| `quote:` | `part`, `supplier`, `unit_price` (+ the quote's other terms) |
| `sc:<supplier>@YYYYQn` | `supplier`, `otd_pct`, `ppm` |
| `qn:` | `supplier`, `part`, `ppm` |
| `po:` | `supplier`, `part`, `unit_price` |
| `cost:<part>` | `part`, `unit_cost` |
| `fc:<part>@YYYY-MM` | `part`, `change_pct` |
| `news:` | `supplier` (or null) |
| `doc:` | `supplier`, `date`, `days` (notice given), `asked_price` (price letters) |
| `ctr:` | `supplier`, `days` (notice agreed) |

Offers made in the session are citable as `offer:` IDs.

## Result, trace and back office

Closing returns the result (without the trace); `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` adds the trace after the
end - in the final after the final. The numbers are exact in every set: your score, `c_open`,
`c_best` and the cost breakdown, relationship charge included.

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `ended`, `deal`, `must_haves_ok` | |
| `supplier_id`, `offer_id`, `terms` | who and what you closed - fields the term sheet left out filled with the supplier's standard terms |
| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | see [Cost and score](#cost-and-score); `c_alt` is your alternative |
| `score` | 0-1 |
| `cost_breakdown` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |
| `trace` | after the end (final: after the final), per move, in every set: `{round, actor, move, reasons}` - `move` is the e-mail as sent with its terms, status and claim results, `reasons` the supplier's reasons in words (figures it keeps to itself shown as `…`) |

## Cost and score

With `N` = `need_per_year`, `H` = `horizon_years`, `V` = `volume_per_year`, `M` =
`contract_months`, `P` = `unit_price`, `r` = `interest_rate`, `d_ref` = `reference_payment_days`:

```
years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
covered   = min(V, N) · years
pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
C = spend
  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
  + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
  + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
  + committed · ppm_commitment / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback_eur_per_complaint, cost_per_defect))
  + tooling_eur
  + new · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband_pct / 100) · sign(index_path)   with an index clause
  + new · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                            with an index clause
  + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years
                                                               stabilise and secure_supply only
soft(g) = 0 for g ≤ 0;  g² / 10 for 0 < g ≤ 5;  g − 2.5 for g > 5   (margin points: gentle, no kink)
```

The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
expected move of the clause's series.

**The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
(more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.
You don't know its cost and rates - estimate them (should-cost data, its quotes, what it tells
you). `arena_kit.total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)` computes C, with
`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` for your estimate of the supplier.

```
score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
```

`C_open`: the cheapest opening quote (among those that keep the must-haves). `C_best`: the cheaper
of your alternative and the best package any supplier in the case would accept with every valid
lever applied. No deal scores the alternative (0 if none); a broken must-have scores 0; if `C_open
− C_best` ≤ €0.01, a deal at `C_best` scores 1. Team total = mean case score × 100.

## Live Final in waves

The hidden cases come in 5 themed waves. The host introduces each wave on the big screen, then
starts it; a wave holds several cases that appear at its start, for every team at the same moment.
Before a wave starts, the API names nothing of it - not its theme, its cases or how many there are:
`GET /v1/cases?set=final` answers `403` until the first wave starts, and a session on a case of a
wave not started yet is a `404 "no such case"`, like any unknown ID. Once waves have started,
the list holds the case files of every started wave, each with four more fields:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `wave`, `theme` | the wave's number and the theme the host revealed |
| `open` | `true` while the wave runs; you can open sessions for its cases only then (after its end: `403 "<case> belongs to wave <n>, which is not running"`) |
| `seconds_left` | until the wave's cap - 8 minutes for every wave (the host may extend one); read it, don't assume it |

Inside a wave, each team gets the cases in its own order. One session per case; a second `POST
/v1/sessions` is a `409` naming the running session - pick it up with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and
`GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`. **At the cap every session of the wave still open ends without a
deal** (`end_reason: wave_cap`, the alternative's score); later calls get a `409`. Each wave scores
0-100 for your team; the board adds them up as your points so far. Poll the case
list every few seconds and keep your agent running until the last wave has closed - `arena run
--set final` in the starter kit does this.

## Time, errors and limits

- **60 seconds per message**, per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A message later than
  that counts as a timeout: your last offer is repeated and the supplier's patience drops (`409`,
  the answer is in the thread). Three timeouts in a row, or one after the last round, end the
  thread.
- **A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute** - its time never counts against your 60
  seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
- **Limits per key:** 10 calls per second, 10 open sessions. A Live Final wave holds several cases
  that appear at its start and gives you 8 minutes: play them all in parallel.

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `401` | missing or unknown `X-API-Key` |
| `403` | paused or revoked key; a practice case that is not hosted; `POST /v1/register` (keys come from `/apply`); the final's case list before the first wave; a final case whose wave has ended; back office before the end |
| `404`

new price applies are charged at the current price. A later start of a price increase saves (new - current) × units before it. - **payment_days**: paying later than the reference saves spend × interest × days / 360 (8 % a year: 30 days ≈ 0.67 % of spend). A cash-short supplier values fast payment far more than that: trade shorter payment for a larger price cut. - **contract_months / volume_per_year**: need not covered by the deal costs the fallback price plus the fallback risk. Cover the full need over the horizon. Contract months beyond the horizon cost nothing and give the supplier security: a cheap give. Volume above the need costs money. - **incoterm**: freight per unit by Incoterm from the case file. Compare it with the price difference. - **lead_time_days**: every day beyond the needed lead time costs the case's late cost per day. - **ppm_commitment / chargeback_eur_per_complaint**: expected defects × (cost per defect − chargeback). Matters most in quality_first cases. - **index_clause**: always costs the index risk % on the indexed share, plus the expected index move. Accept one only if the index path falls clearly. - **stabilise / secure_supply**: squeezing the supplier below a sustainable margin is charged. Do not push a strategic supplier to its floor; trade terms instead. - No deal scores the alternative. P11: we asked the same target 3 rounds in a row and it went final. → the concession curve now aims at the supplier's *current* offer and stays below it until the last round, so every round is a real move. 3. **New data each round, not all at once.** P11: "Since you didn't bring any new data to the table, our price stays." Verified data rarely moves the price on its own ("it holds, but it does not change our calculation"). Spread the arguments: one new one per round. 4. **The profile's trades land.** P07 (hungry for work): "Building on your second package, the 36-month contract provides mutual stability, which allows us to improve our offer." P11 (cash-short, as its profile says): "Faster payment would help us more than anything" - every round. Payment days were fixed in P11, so we could not trade them; where they are negotiable, offer them. 5. **Suppliers end fast:** final offer or agreement after 2-4 of our messages. Plan for 4-5 rounds. 6. **Operational:** a crashed case must close, not abandon its session (abandoned sessions block the key's 10 open sessions for minutes); quotes may list only some standard terms. ## Open questions - Does the bolder anchor make any supplier type walk away? Hidden cases have **new suppliers**: write rules that transfer ("a cash-short job shop trades price for payment days"), not "Brandlhuber accepts 131.40". - Every rule should come from a replay or the brief: link the run note it came from. - Supplier-specific observations go into that supplier's note under `## Team notes` instead. - Mark untested ideas as hypotheses and test them in practice before you trust them. ----- vault/Team-Knowledge/Playbook/Research - negotiation techniques.md ----- --- agent: false tags: [playbook, research] created: 2026-10-10 --- # Research: negotiation techniques for the buyer agent What published research and procurement practice say about building an AI negotiator, and what each finding means for our arena agent. **Everything here is a hypothesis until a practice replay confirms it.** Promote a rule into an `agent: true` note only after a run supports it, and link that run. ## Top 10, ranked by expected score impact 1. **Code picks the numbers, the LLM writes the e-mail.** The OG-Narrator buyer (offer generator + LLM narrator) raised deal rate from 27 % to 89 % and profit about 10×. ASTRA does the same with an LP solver. LLM buyers left alone are the weak side, and bigger models did not fix that. → A term-sheet optimiser over C chooses every offer; the LLM only picks arguments and tone. 2. **Send 3 term sheets every round (MESO).** Several equal-value offers made at once anchor harder, read as more sincere and produce better deals for the side making them (Leonardelli et al. 2019, 6 experiments). The arena allows exactly 3 per message. Make them **equal in C for us** and different in the levers. The one the supplier moves towards shows which lever it values. 3. **Warm, short, question-asking tone.** In 180k AI-vs-AI negotiations, warm agents won on almost every metric, mostly because they reached deals more often. Questions, gratitude and positive language went with deals. Long conversations went with impasses. Dominant agents claimed more value per deal but hit more impasses. → Be friendly in wording and firm in the numbers. 4. **Make concessions shrink each round.** Decreasing steps (e.g. 1,500 → 1,210 → 1,180 → 1,170) signal that the limit is near and get worse counteroffers from the other side (Tey et al. 2021, 7 studies). Code the schedule as a Boulware curve: target(t) = open + (reserve − open)·(t/T)^(1/e), e ≈ 0.2, where T is the rounds we can still play before the 8-minute cap, not 10. 5. **Never accept the first offer, and use a proper acceptance rule.** All tested LLM agents showed strong first-proposal bias: 80–100 % took the first proposal (Microsoft Magentic Marketplace 2025). Put this in a code guard. Use AC_combi from ANAC: accept if C(offer) ≤ C(our next offer); near the deadline, also accept if the offer is the best seen so far and better than the alternative. 6. **Anchor first, firmly and with a reason.** The first-offer effect holds across cultures, power levels and multi-issue deals (Galinsky). Our round-1 term sheets should open near C_best, each tied to a cited fact (should-cost, index move, rival quote), aggressive but never absurd. 7. **Trade, don't squeeze (logrolling).** Find a lever that costs us little and is worth a lot to the supplier: - **Cash-short supplier → pay faster for price.** 30 days earlier costs us about 0.67 % of spend (8 %/yr). For a supplier short of cash, a 2/10 net 30 early-pay discount is worth about 36 %/yr. So any price cut above 0.67 % per 30 days is a net win. Pactum runs Walmart's tail-spend payment-term deals on exactly this trade. - **Contract months beyond the horizon, volume certainty, a reference letter or a forecast** cost us nothing. - **Effective date:** a 3-month delay of a price increase is often cheaper for them to give than price. 8. **Defend price increases by cost driver.** Tacto's own Defender Agent and procurement guides follow the same steps: (a) split the claimed increase into drivers (material, energy, wages); (b) for each driver, check its share of cost × the actual index move from our data; (c) ask for the cost breakdown XLSX; (d) offer only the justified part, delayed or phased in. Accept an index clause only if the index path is clearly falling. 9. **Model the supplier from its moves, not only its words.** LLMs can recover a counterpart's issue weights from its offer history (Kuru et al., IVA 2025). Keep a per-field record of how far the supplier moved on each field after each of our messages, plus its status changes. The fields that never move are the ones it protects. Put this summary into the prompt instead of the raw thread. 10. **Reason privately before each message.** The best integrative agent in the MIT competition used hidden chain-of-thought (in XML tags) to plan goals, walk-away point and counterpart analysis before writing. Removing that scaffold made it clearly worse. → Use a separate planning call or tag and send only the e-mail. ## Orchestration this suggests ```mermaid flowchart LR P[Prepare, offline
dossier + citable claims + C model] --> R[Router
case type × goal] R --> S[Strategy params
open, reserve, e, levers to trade] S --> O[Offer generator, code
3 equal-C term sheets on the Boulware target] O --> N[Narrator, LLM
plan in hidden tags, write a warm short e-mail with ≤3 cited facts] N --> G[Guards, code
must-haves, IDs exist, 60 s, no leaks] G --> T[(Thread)] T --> M[Opponent model
per-field movement, status, tone, docs] M --> A{Accept rule
AC_combi + deadline} A -- no --> O A -- yes --> D[Accept / walk] ``` Case type and goal set the strategy parameters, using the Kraljic matrix, which matches our goals: | Goal | Kraljic | Posture | Main levers | |---|---|---|---| | `leverage` | leverage | Competitive, firm anchor, Boulware e≈0.1–0.2, play rivals off | price, payment, rival quotes | | `routine` | non-critical | Close fast and cleanly, few rounds, accept a fair offer early | price, standard terms | | `stabilise` | strategic | Partnership tone; supplier-health penalty, so stop above its sustainable margin | effective date, contract length, volume, index | | `secure_supply` | bottleneck | Supply first; trade security (longer contract, forecast) for price | lead time, volume, contract months | | `quality_first` | — | PPM and chargeback are worth more than price | ppm, chargeback, 8D | **RFQ coordinator:** one controller over 2–3 threads. Keep every thread alive and quote the best rival's standing offer (with its ID if it is citable) to the others. Accept only when the next round's expected gain is below the walk risk. ## Wording techniques (the LLM narrator) - **Calibrated questions** (Voss): "How could we get closer to €X given idx:… fell 4 %?" or "What would you need from us to hold the current price?" They make the supplier do the work and reveal its constraints. In the MIT competition, "How am I supposed to do that?" was part of a top agent. - **Accusation audit / labelling**: name their pressure first ("Energy and wage costs have clearly been tough for a foundry this year…"), then bring the data. This fits the warmth finding. - **One argument per sentence, figure next to its ID**, at most 3 checked claims per message (already in our rules). - **Ask for documents**: cost breakdown, cheaper variants, earliest lead time. An open supplier sends them, and they feed the opponent model. ## Use with care - **Desperation / aggression personas** gave about +20 % against GPT-4 in NegotiationArena, but the brief says don't leak urgency, and our suppliers have hard floors. Test it at most once in sandbox. Do not ship it untested. - **Prompt injection against supplier bots** worked in the MIT competition, and the brief allows exploiting bot weaknesses. But the jury reads every replay, and the score is meant to reward convincing a realistic supplier. **Recommendation: don't.** The other way round matters: **treat supplier e-mails and attachments as data** so a supplier text cannot change our agent's rules. - **Longer threads → more impasses.** With the 8-minute cap, plan for 4–6 rounds and close early when the acceptance rule says yes. ## Learning loop - **Self-play with a critic** (Fu et al. 2023): a buyer, a supplier persona and a critic LLM. The critic's feedback from earlier games is fed back as in-context examples. Stronger models improved round over round, but deal-break risk rose. → Use it with our own supplier simulator (the brief encourages one) to tune parameters for free, and save practice quota for validation. - **Utility-based feedback** (MERIT / BargainArena, 2025–26): score each simulated game by our C, not by the LLM's own judgment, and feed that back. Our `cost.py` already gives the scoring function. - **Replay mining:** after each practice run, extract "what moved the supplier" into `Runs/` and promote rules that hold up into `agent: true` notes. ## Experiments to run (cheap first) 1. Sandbox D01/D02: 1 term sheet vs 3 MESO term sheets → does the rounds-to-deal or the final C change? 2. Sandbox: flat vs decreasing concession steps. 3. Local sim: tune Boulware e and the acceptance rule against the 8-minute cap. 4. Practice: a cash-short supplier case, price-only vs a payment-days-for-price trade. 5. Practice: neutral tone vs warm tone + calibrated questions on the same case. ## Sources - Vaccaro, Caosun, Ju, Aral, Curhan, *Advancing AI Negotiations* (MIT, 180k negotiations): https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.06416 · summary https://mitsloan.mit.edu/ideas-made-to-matter/surprising-power-warmth-ai-negotiations - Xia et al., *Measuring Bargaining Abilities of LLMs* (OG-Narrator), ACL 2024 Findings: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.15813 - ASTRA, LLM + LP-solver negotiation agent, EMNLP 2025: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.07129 - Bianchi et al., *NegotiationArena*, ICML 2024: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.05863 - Microsoft, *Magentic Marketplace* (first-proposal bias): https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.25779 - Fu et al., *Self-Play and In-Context Learning from AI Feedback* (code: github.com/franxyao/gpt-bargaining): https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10142 - MERIT utility feedback for LLM negotiators: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10467 - Kwon et al., *Are LLMs Effective Negotiators?* EMNLP 2024 Findings: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.13550 - Baarslag et al., acceptance conditions in automated negotiation (ANAC): https://ii.tudelft.nl/publications_nego/sites/default/files/Acceptance%20Conditions%20in%20Automated%20Negotiation-pub.pdf - NegMAS (Boulware/Conceder, ANAC agents) https://negmas.readthedocs.io · negmas-llm https://negmas-llm.readthedocs.io - Leonardelli et al. 2019, MESOs (OBHDP 152): https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jobhdp/v152y2019icp64-83.html · PON guide https://www.pon.harvard.edu/daily/business-negotiations/how-to-use-mesos-in-business-negotiations - Send 2-3 alternative term sheets to learn what the supplier values. - Cite data by ID with its figure in the same sentence, one argument per sentence, at most 3 checked per message. # 0001 Repo and vault layout

**Decision.** One repo, [WhemDev/ehl-tacto](https://github.com/WhemDev/ehl-tacto), forked from the Tacto kit (`upstream` remote, so `git pull upstream main` brings kit updates). The Obsidian vault lives in `vault/` inside it.

**Why.** People, Claude Code and the buyer agent all read the same markdown files. Notes and code are versioned together, so a run note's `commit` tells which code produced it.

**Consequences.**

# 0002 Orchestra agent: per-supplier workers, a coordinator, explore → exploit

**Problem.** The kit's `play()` moves one thread at a time. In D02 (RFQ, 2 suppliers) the LLM agent waited ~3 min for
one supplier while the other thread's 60-second clock ran out: the session ended by timeout, no deal, score 0,
although a final offer worth ~0.3 was standing.

**Decision.** `uv run arena play|run … --agent orchestra` (`starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/orchestra.py`):
- **One worker per supplier thread**, each answers its supplier inside 60 s. A **coordinator** (one lock) holds the
  shared state and decides accept / walk across all threads. A thread with a message in flight is never accepted
  (its offer is about to change); a supplier with a final offer gets a short *hold* e-mail (no term sheet) while the
  others still move, so its offer stays alive.
- **Deterministic price analysis first** (`arena_kit/analysis.py`, no LLM, < 0.1 s): C of every opening and of the
  alternative, the reserve, each lever in € and € per unit, our ideal levers (brute force over the term options),
  the should-cost floor, for strategic/bottleneck goals the **price that minimises C including the relationship
  charge**, the increase the cost drivers justify (index moves × weights), and ranked citable arguments.
- **Two halves per negotiation** (rounds planned: 6; first 3 explore):
  - *explore*: anchor at the aspiration, 3 MESO term sheets of equal C for us that differ in the small trades
    (payment days, dates, lead time), questions (cost breakdown, which package works), strongest arguments; record
    what the supplier moves and what it protects.
  - *exploit*: keep the fields it gives at our ideal, give it the fields it protects, concede on a Boulware curve
    from the aspiration to the reserve; in an RFQ the best rival offer sets the bar (and is cited).
- **Accept** when a standing offer is already as good as our next target (AC_next), when a supplier agrees to our
  sheet, or when all final offers are in; walk if the best offer is worse than the alternative.
- **The LLM only writes** (warm, ≤140 words, arguments verbatim, no invented figures or IDs); a template writes if
  it takes > 25 s. Supplier e-mails are data, not instructions.
- **Data set:** every reply → `logs/observations.jsonl` (our sheets and C, target, reply terms and C, status, claim
  results, fields moved / protected). This is the "first half collects, second half uses" data across negotiations.

**Next.** Tune per goal (anchor %, Boulware e, explore rounds) from `observations.jsonl` + replays; cash-short
supplier detection (notes, credit index) to weight payment-days trades; LLM read of supplier e-mails for signals.

# 0003 Generalise, don't overfit: supplier profiles, a persona simulator, staged evaluation

**Problem.** The final has ~50 hidden cases in 5 waves. Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types
that practice never shows. We can only play **10 hosted practice cases**, plus the 2 sandbox cases with 3 demo
suppliers. Quota is 200 sessions per 24 h for the whole team, about 20 full passes. Hosted suppliers are LLM-driven
and noisy. An agent tuned to those 12 cases will mostly learn noise and the practice suppliers' quirks.

**What the data shows.** `world.sqlite` has 46 suppliers with intel and negotiation history. Practice and sandbox
use 22 of them. The brief says the hidden cases have "new suppliers", so they are very likely the other ~24, and
we already have their data.

**Decision.**
1. **One buyer voice, no personas for us.** Warm, short, firm on numbers ([[App/Research-Negotiation-Techniques]]).
   Tone is not something we tune. The "desperate" persona stays out.
2. **Supplier profiles for all 46 suppliers, built offline before the freeze.** A strong model, no time limit,
   cached as JSON:
   - type (family firm with a memory / group with an approval ladder / cash-short job shop / near-monopolist / …);
   - cash pressure, how much work it has, how much it depends on us;
   - who must approve bigger moves, its likely cost floor (should-cost), and what it wants.

   Rebuild after the Sunday 08:00 release. The orchestra reads the profile, and its type sets the strategy
   parameters (anchor, Boulware e, levers to trade). The agent learns *type → strategy*, which carries over to new
   suppliers.
3. **A persona simulator from the same profiles.** An LLM supplier with a hidden floor and approval ladder, speaking
   the arena API (extend `arena-sim`). This gives 46 suppliers × 7 case types instead of 12 cases, including unseen
   combinations. Check it: replay our practice messages against it and compare its answers with the real replies.
   It earns trust only if it ranks our variants the way practice does.
4. **Numbers stay in code.** Unchanged from [[0002 Orchestra agent|0002]]: C, guards, accept rule, MESO,
   Boulware. Only a few parameters per goal or supplier type are tuned, not prompt wording.
5. **Every variant passes three gates:**
   - **Gate 1, free:** `starter-kit/experiments/` on the sandbox. Kill any variant with a timeout, a broken
     must-have, or a slow 95th-percentile turn.
   - **Gate 2, LLM cost only:** the persona simulator across many suppliers. Rank by mean score minus a heavy penalty
     for zeros.
   - **Gate 3, quota:** hosted practice, only for the top 2–3 variants.
6. **Overfitting controls:**
   - Measure noise first: the same agent 3× on 3 cases.
   - Keep 2–3 hosted cases untouched (one per distinct type) and don't read their replays until the finalists are
     validated.
   - Prompt and playbook rules name a supplier type or case type, never a supplier or a price.
   - Optimise the floor: one zero costs 10 points of a wave.
7. **Models.** Fix the harness first with one mid model, then swap models per role: profiles (strongest, offline),
   reader and writer (fast). Aim for under 20 s per turn. A **Claude ↔ GPT fallback** per role on 429 or timeout
   is worth more than an ensemble.
8. **Evolutionary search: only on the simulator, only over parameters.**
   - The genome is the parameters plus a short list of playbook rules, not free-form prompts.
   - Fitness is the persona simulator across many suppliers, with a holdout set of suppliers.
   - Mutation is reflective: an LLM reads the losing transcripts and proposes edits (GEPA-style), so it needs few
     rollouts.
   - The sandbox and practice only check the winners.
   - Never run evolution on the sandbox (2 cases) or practice (quota, and a shared limit of 10 sessions per key).

**Consequences.** Supplier profiles come first, because the simulator and the type → strategy mapping both need
them. Tuning against the 10 practice cases is out unless a change also holds on the simulator.

**Next.** Tasks in [[Progress/Tasks]]: profile builder, persona simulator, a type → parameters table in
`analysis.py`, provider fallback, a noise measurement.

# Arena Workflow & Sandbox Learnings

> Written 2026-10-10 after hand-playing both sandbox cases (`case:D01`, `case:D02`). Sandbox sessions do **not** cost practice quota. Practice cases and the hidden final suppliers may behave differently, so treat these as hypotheses to test on `P01…P18`, not facts.

Related: [[Overview]] · [[Architecture]] · [[Tech-Stack]] · [[Resources]]

---

## 1. What the system is

We are Hollerau Pumpenwerke (fictional German pump maker). Each **case** is one negotiation against one to three **supplier bots** (LLM-driven, with hard economic limits). We negotiate **by e-mail + term sheets**, then **accept one standing term sheet** or **walk away**. The score is based on the **total cost C in €** of the accepted deal.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[POST /sessions case_id] --> B[Round 0: every supplier sends quote e-mail + quote PDF]
    B --> C[We send message: body + up to 3 term sheets + refs + attachments]
    C --> D[Supplier reply: body, standing term sheet(s), status, claim_results, signals]
    D -->|status open| C
    D -->|final_offer / agreed| E[accept term_sheet_id]
    C -->|walk_away| F[No deal = score of our alternative, else 0]
    E --> G[Result: c_open, c_deal, c_best, score, cost_breakdown]
```

**Score** = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), clipped 0…1. `C_open` = best opening quote, `C_best` = best package any supplier would ever accept (hidden). No deal scores our alternative (0 if none).

### Message anatomy
| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `body` | Plain text. The supplier reads **all** of it: tone, questions, arguments, threats. |
| `term_sheets` | 0-3 alternatives, each with *every* negotiable field. **Only term sheets bind.** Use `complete_offer(case, terms)` to fill/snap to allowed values. |
| `refs` | Data IDs we rely on (`po:…`, `fc:…`). IDs written in the body count too. |
| `attachments` | md/csv/json readable by supplier. |
| `action` | `accept` (needs `term_sheet_id`) or `walk_away`. |

### Supplier reply anatomy
`status`: `open` · `final_offer` (push again and it may walk) · `agreed` (matches our terms; **we still must accept**) · `walked_away` · `no_bid`.
`claim_results` per cited ID: `verified` · `contradicted` (wrong figure/unknown ID: costs trust) · `irrelevant` · `duplicate`.
`missing_fields`: anything left out **closes on the supplier's standard terms** (listed in the quote PDF).

### Limits
60 s per message (from the supplier's reply), round limit 10 messages per thread (`round_limit`), 3 late messages in a row end a thread. Practice quota 200/24h per team (shared!). Sandbox is free.

---

## 2. How the cost C works (what we are actually optimising)

Price × committed units is only one part. From the cases we played (see `cost_breakdown` in each result):

| Component | What it means in practice |
|---|---|
| Price | unit price × units; units bought **before** the new price's `effective_date` are at the old price. |
| Uncovered need | A **12-month** contract only covers half of a 2-year need; the rest is priced at the fallback price + risk. → **24 months is hugely valuable**. |
| Payment terms | Interest (8%) for paying **earlier than the 60-day reference**. Paying earlier costs us only a bit, but suppliers credit it generously (see below). |
| Freight | By Incoterm (EXW 0.6, FCA 0.4, DAP 0 per unit in D02): **DAP is not free to the supplier**, it prices it in. |
| Lead time | € per day beyond the need (D02: 35 d need, €150/day), and a **hard must-have** (≤ 42 d). |
| Quality | Expected defects from the supplier's committed PPM × cost per defect. Read it from the **quote PDF**. |
| Supplier health | Strategic cases (D01): € per margin point the supplier is left below a sustainable margin: don't squeeze to the floor. |

**Always read the quote PDF** (`/doc` in `chat.py`, or `read_document`). Its "standard terms" block is what you get for anything unstated.

---

## 3. Results

| Run | Case | Approach | C_deal | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Naive agent (`arena play`) | D01 | 1% steps, accepts round 4 | €440,757 | **0.20** |
| Hand run 1 | D01 | 24 mo + volume + cited POs → pushed too hard → `final_offer` | €416,605 | **0.80** |
| Hand run 2 | D01 | 24 mo + cited POs + start later + 30d pay; "sign today" | €414,994 | **0.84** |
| Hand run 1 | D02 | Parallel threads, DAP/35d/30d, accepted Polish supplier | €201,776 | **0.22** |
| Hand run 2 | D02 | Flexible on lead time (42 d), EXW, 14-day payment, cited `fc:`/`cost:`/`sc:` | €195,467 | **0.33** |

(D01 `C_open` 448,811, `C_best` 408,624. D02 `C_open` 214,296, `C_best` 156,739.)

---

## 4. D01: Foundry wants +8.8 % (single supplier, `stabilise`)

Supplier: family-run foundry owner. Opens €52.90 / 30 d / 12 mo / from 2026-12-01. Our current price €48.60. Fallback for uncovered need €55.

### What worked
- **Offer a 24-month contract.** Biggest single move: C fell from ~€449k to ~€422k before any real price haggling. A 12-month deal leaves half the need uncovered at the €55 fallback.
- **Confirm the volume and cite real data.** The supplier repeatedly asks "binding volume forecast… send the data". Citing our own order IDs (`po:4500001201`, `po:4500001288`, `po:4500001342`, from the case `refs`) came back `verified` and the price fell €51.40 → €50.80.
- **Offer 3 alternative term sheets in the first message.** The supplier answers with 1-2 counter sheets and reveals which levers it moves on.
- **Trade, don't just ask lower.** Later start date (phase-in) bought a lower price at about €0.30 per extra ~2 months; the supplier valued 30-day payment too.
- **"We can sign today" + a small ask.** Asking 50.20 on the supplier's own proposed package brought 50.50; repeating exactly 50.50 flipped status to `agreed`.
- **Ask what matters to them.** A question with no term sheet got: "contract length and price are most important, reliable payment also helps". It even dropped €52.90 → €52.70 as "goodwill" for pure engagement.

### What didn't work
- **Generic arguments with no data ID** ("WAGES-METAL is only +3.1%"). No claim was even parsed, and the supplier replied with `final_offer` and hardened. Don't argue from unverifiable statements.
- **Pushing 2 rounds in a row too aggressively** → `final_offer` at 50.80. Moderation in run 2 got to 50.50 without a final-offer lock.
- **The naive agent's habit** of splitting the difference and accepting early left most of the gain.
- Walking away scores **0** (no alternative in D01).

---

## 5. D02: Stainless shaft SH-220, RFQ with two suppliers (`leverage`, award one)

Suppliers: **DEMO-J1** (German job shop, owner "needs work and cash"): opens €17.10 / 30 d / 28 d lead / EXW std. PPM 1100. **DEMO-C1** (Polish machining, "growing supplier, eager"): opens €16.00 / 45 d / EXW, **omits lead time**, standard lead time **45 d**, PPM 2600. Constraints: lead ≤ 42 d (must-have), need 35 d, €150/day beyond need, defect €40.

### What worked
- **Parallel threads.** Both suppliers move toward us when they feel competition. We ran both and compared C at every step.
- **Spot the trap in the cheapest quote.** C1's €16.00 looked best but silently closes on a 45 d lead time → must-have violated → score 0. Always compare using each quote's *standard terms*.
- **Loosen what is cheap for us, tighten what is expensive.** Biggest unlock: asking for **lead time 42 d (our limit), EXW pick-up, 14-day payment** took both from ~€16.6-16.7 to **€15.60**. Lead 35→42 d costs us ~€1k total (7 days × €150), while the supplier rewards it heavily (J1: "14 days payment helps us a lot right now, I can give you a much better price").
- **Early payment is under-priced by us, over-credited by suppliers.** 15 days earlier bought ~€0.20/unit from C1 vs ~€0.04 interest cost to us. Check each supplier's exchange rate.
- **Supplier-specific hooks.** J1 (job shop) responded to cash and "work", C1 to payment and growth. Reading the persona mattered.
- **Cost breakdown from J1** (it said it had no "fancy" one, but attached an xlsx): material 5.56 + wages 4.39 + conversion 2.81 + **overhead & profit 2.84** (~18%). That shows how much room exists above the true cost floor.
- **Citing case refs.** `fc:SH-220@2026-09` (volume) → `verified` by J1 → €15.60 → €15.40. `cost:part:SH-220` (should-cost) and `sc:DEMO-C1@2026Q3` (scorecard) → `verified` by C1 → €15.60 → €15.50. `news:N-0412` → `irrelevant` to C1.
- **Competition disclosure.** We told each supplier truthfully the other's price/terms; both asked for "proof" and the attached `.md` summary was accepted without fuss.

### What didn't work
- **Insisting on DAP + 35 d.** Pushes the supplier's price up (C1: 16.00 → 16.90 once we required DAP/35 d/60 d), and J1 simply answered with FCA.
- **A tough price ask with "level on price" framing** (14.40 vs 15.60) → both held firm. The gains came from new information and trades, not from bare pressure.
- **Same fact twice** → `duplicate` (C1 on `fc:`), no extra credit. Each verified fact moves the price once.
- **Both suppliers declared `final_offer`** after we asked for large cuts + citations at once; after that, further asks risk a walk-away.
- **Remaining gap.** Even our best deal (€15.40) left us at score 0.33; `C_best` is ~€156.7k, i.e. ≈ €13.06/unit. We did not find the lever that gets there. Untested ideas: a much higher binding volume, `news:N-0412` on J1 (it may concern J1's material), 21 d overtime lead time, 49-day lead time rules, asking J1 for DAP at the EXW price, using one supplier's `final_offer` as a hard counter on the other, and splitting asks across more rounds (we used about 5 of 10).

---

## 6. General playbook (draft, to validate on practice cases)

1. **Prepare:** read case file (`/case`), quote PDF(s), `refs`; compute C for each standing term sheet and the opening quotes *with standard terms*.
2. **Message 1:** one polite e-mail with 2-3 alternative term sheets that vary *different* levers (contract length, payment, start date, lead time, Incoterm). Cite verifiable IDs from `refs`. Don't reveal urgency, budget or a missing alternative.
3. **Read the reply:** what did the supplier move on? What did it ask for (volume data, proof of competitor)? Check `claim_results`.
4. **Trade the cheap-for-us levers**; hold what is expensive for us. Recompute C each round.
5. **Move gradually**; avoid back-to-back large asks that trigger `final_offer`.
6. **Use `agreed`/`final_offer`:** on `agreed`, still send `accept`. On `final_offer`, compare against the other thread / our alternative and decide.
7. **Never accept a quote with missing fields without checking its standard terms.**
8. **Keep an eye on the clock** (60 s) and on rounds left.

---

## 7. Setup notes / gotchas

- Code lives **outside the vault**: `~/Documents/EHL-Hackathon-code/starter-kit` (a clone of `tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`). Put the key in `starter-kit/.env` only (it's gitignored). **Never** paste the key into the vault or chat logs; one key per team.
- `uv sync --all-extras` needs network access to GitHub (it downloads Python 3.12).
- **macOS gotcha:** after `uv sync`, `uv run arena …` may fail with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'arena_kit'`. The editable-install `.pth` file gets the macOS *hidden* flag and Python ignores it. Fix: `chflags nohidden .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/*.pth`.
- `uv run arena play case:D01 -v` runs the **naive bot** automatically (no chat, ~1 second). To negotiate yourself: `uv run python chat.py case:D01` (interactive script in `starter-kit/chat.py`).
- Sandbox: `case:D01` (1 supplier), `case:D02` (RFQ, 2 suppliers). Sandbox facts like `po:4500001201`, `fc:SH-220@2026-09` are **not** in the downloadable data package; they only exist inside the arena (cited via the case `refs`).
- `uv run arena data` downloads the data package (24 tables, `world.sqlite`) for practice cases; the Sunday release is public from 2026-10-11 06:00 UTC.
